recents-read-failed: Recent-project user-settings read failure. $1 is the exact OS settings path; $2 is untranslated technical detail. Both are isolated by the caller. Not a novel-file failure.
recents-save-failed: Recent-project user-settings write failure. $1 is the exact OS settings path; $2 is untranslated technical detail. Both are isolated by the caller. No project folder is deleted.
recents-invalid: Malformed JSON or schema-invalid recent-project settings are preserved at the original path, not silently reset or archived. $1 is that exact isolated OS path; $2 is isolated untranslated validation detail.
error-workspace-folder-inspection-failed: Filesystem inspection could not establish folder availability or project nesting. $1 is the exact isolated OS path that failed (possibly an ancestor marker or descendant folder); $2 is isolated untranslated technical detail. Also used when checking recent-project availability; do not imply files were changed.
error-workspace-folder-search-limit: The project-nesting search stopped while folders remained to inspect, so initialization is refused. $1 is the exact isolated chosen root; $2 is the unchanged numeric folder visit limit. Recommend choosing a smaller folder, not increasing permissions or deleting files.
error-workspace-folder-dialog-failed: The operating system's native folder chooser failed. Cancellation is not an error. $1 is isolated untranslated original technical detail.
recents-remember-failed: Non-blocking warning after successful project open/initialization when recording recents failed. $1 is the localized specific failure with technical details. Do not imply the project failed to open or manuscript saving failed.
placement-order-invalid: Local inspector validation for a non-integer order. Order is the numeric manuscript position, not a date or word count. No save is attempted for this value.
placement-missing-order: Brief unordered-chapter reason, also inserted into placement-not-in-book: the chapter needs a numeric order.
placement-no-part: Brief unordered-chapter reason, also inserted into placement-not-in-book: the book has parts but this chapter has no part link.
placement-part-not-a-link: Brief unordered-chapter reason, also inserted into placement-not-in-book: the part frontmatter value is not a usable wikilink.
placement-part-not-found: Brief unordered-chapter reason, also inserted into placement-not-in-book: the linked part cannot be found.
placement-part-ambiguous: Brief unordered-chapter reason, also inserted into placement-not-in-book: the part link resolves to multiple candidates.
placement-not-in-book: Complete inspector placement sentence. $1 is a translated placement reason, not user text; the chapter file still exists, but is outside the numbered manuscript.
placement-clash: Complete duplicate-order sentence shared by inspector and binder warning tooltip/accessibility text. $1 is the numeric order as text; $2 is an already-quoted localized list of sibling chapter titles. Do not imply files are modified.
placement-quoted-title: Quotes around one sibling chapter title in a placement clash. $1 is the exact user title isolated by the caller; do not translate or normalize it.
tabs-notice-load-failed: User settings storage could not be read for document tabs. Navigation remains usable for this app session; this is not a manuscript-read failure.
tabs-notice-invalid: Malformed or schema-invalid saved tab metadata. Starts fresh navigation state, not a new novel; no manuscript text is deleted.
tabs-notice-save-failed: Document-tab metadata could not be persisted. Current session navigation still works. This does not describe saving manuscript text.
tabs-notice-pruned: Inactive open documents absent from the current listing were removed from the tab strip, not deleted from disk. An active missing draft is retained.
preferences-notice-load-failed: Writing display/navigation preferences could not be read from user settings. Defaults are used without altering novel files.
preferences-notice-invalid: Malformed or schema-invalid writing preferences. Defaults are used; the saved settings are not replaced until an explicit preference change.
preferences-notice-save-failed: Writing display/navigation settings could not be persisted, but changes remain in memory for this session. Not a manuscript-save failure.
link-wiki-unresolved: Temporary notice for a wikilink with no unique resolved target (missing or ambiguous). $1 is the exact written target, isolated by the caller. Keep folder-disambiguation advice; do not imply file deletion.
link-markdown-unresolved: Temporary notice for a Markdown link with no resolved project file. $1 is the exact written address, isolated by the caller; do not translate or normalize it.
link-target-unsupported: Refusal to open a resolved link target unsupported by the editor. $1 is the exact project-relative path, isolated by the caller. No file is modified.
reference-open-failed: Fallback for a failed explicit Open in editor action from the reference panel when no more specific editor notice exists.
language-label: Label for the app-wide interface-language selector, not manuscript language.
language-save-failed: Visible failure after saving language preferences fails. The previous locale remains active.
language-load-failed: Startup warning when preferences cannot be read. Supported system language is used, otherwise English.
language-invalid-settings: Startup warning for malformed or unsupported saved preferences. The original file is not changed on load.
language-incomplete: Temporary Hebrew foundation notice: complete translation and RTL qualification are not yet finished.
language-incomplete-label: Disclosure summary for the temporary incomplete-Hebrew-support notice.
welcome-tagline: Welcome-screen description. Markdown is the file format name.
open-folder: Button that opens the native project-folder chooser.
project-overview-label: Eyebrow label above the project title in the editor's empty-document overview.
project-overview-hint: Guidance to select a chapter in the binder before writing.
project-overview-contents: Heading for the generated project file-kind counts.
project-overview-empty: Empty state when the project overview contains no Markdown files.
project-overview-count-part: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-chapter: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-character: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-location: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-note: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-outline: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-scene: Project overview count noun. $1 is the raw numeric count used for plural selection; the formatted number is displayed separately.
project-overview-count-untyped: Project overview count noun for a Markdown file with no recognized type. $1 is the raw plural-selection count; the formatted number is displayed separately.
chrome-location: Accessible name of the project breadcrumb navigation.
chrome-view: Accessible name of the main-view tab list.
chrome-binder: Accessible name of the binder toggle.
chrome-inspector: Accessible name of the properties inspector toggle.
chrome-focus: Accessible name of the focus-mode toggle.
chrome-binder-tooltip: Binder toggle tooltip. $1 is the unchanged isolated keyboard shortcut.
chrome-inspector-tooltip: Inspector toggle tooltip. $1 is the unchanged isolated keyboard shortcut.
chrome-focus-tooltip: Focus-mode toggle tooltip. $1 is the unchanged isolated keyboard shortcut.
chrome-leave-focus: Focus-mode exit button. $1 is the unchanged isolated Escape key label.
chrome-save-read-only: Save indicator when the project is read-only; takes precedence over draft save state.
chrome-save-saved: Save indicator: current text has been saved.
chrome-save-unsaved: Save indicator: the writer is editing unsaved text.
chrome-save-saving: Save indicator: saving is in progress.
chrome-save-conflict: Save indicator: outside changes prevent saving; do not imply the draft was discarded.
chrome-save-missing: Save indicator: the source file is missing and the draft is not saved.
chrome-count-part: Complete word-count sentence for the open part. $1 is the raw count for PLURAL only; $2 is its UI-locale formatted number, including zero.
chrome-count-chapter: Complete word-count sentence for the open chapter. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-character: Complete word-count sentence for the open character entry. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-location: Complete word-count sentence for the open location entry. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-note: Complete word-count sentence for the open note. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-template: Complete word-count sentence for the open template. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-outline: Complete word-count sentence for the open outline. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-words: Focus-mode count. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count. Zero must be displayed as a number, not a dash.
chrome-count-manuscript: Whole manuscript count. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the formatted count.
chrome-count-named-part: Current part title/count. $1 is the raw plural selector; $2 is the exact isolated untrusted title; $3 is the formatted count. No HTML.
appearance-trigger: Short label for the writing-appearance popover button.
appearance-heading: Heading and accessible trigger name for the writing-appearance popover.
appearance-close-label: Accessible name for closing the writing-appearance popover.
appearance-close: Visible close button in writing appearance.
appearance-hint: Appearance changes affect display only, never manuscript words.
appearance-size: Label of the prose font-size slider.
appearance-width: Label of the prose line-width slider.
appearance-direction: Label for the writing-surface direction preference; independent of UI language.
appearance-direction-auto: Auto option: choose text direction independently for each prose line.
appearance-direction-ltr: Force left-to-right direction for the whole writing surface.
appearance-direction-rtl: Force right-to-left direction for the whole writing surface.
appearance-pixels: Font-size output. $1 is the UI-locale formatted number of CSS pixels.
appearance-characters: Line-width output. $1 is the UI-locale formatted width in CSS ch units (the font's zero-glyph advance), not a hard character limit.
appearance-all-projects: Scope reminder: writing appearance preferences apply to all projects.
appearance-reset: Button resetting prose size and width to defaults.
tabs-open-documents: Accessible label of the document-navigation section.
tabs-document-list: Accessible name of the document tabs tablist.
tabs-writing: State marker for the protected Writing target tab.
tabs-pinned: State marker for a tab the user chose to keep available.
tabs-preview: State marker for a temporary tab that may be replaced by the next preview.
tabs-missing: State marker for an open document whose file is unavailable. The draft remains protected.
tabs-close-label: Accessible close-button name. $1 is the exact isolated document title, not translated.
tabs-return-title: Return-to-writing tooltip. $1 is the isolated unchanged keyboard shortcut.
tabs-return: Visible action returning to the protected Writing target.
tabs-keep-open: Action converting a temporary preview tab into a retained tab.
tabs-writing-pin-tooltip: Pin tooltip while this tab is the protected Writing target.
tabs-pin-tooltip: Pin tooltip for an ordinary document tab.
tabs-unpin: Action to unpin the active document tab.
tabs-pin: Action to pin the active document tab.
tabs-write-here: Action making the active eligible manuscript entry the Writing target.
tabs-close-other-tooltip: Tooltip for closing eligible unpinned tabs; the current document, Writing target, and pinned tabs remain.
side-tablist: Accessible name of the Manuscript/Codex sidebar tablist.
side-manuscript: Sidebar tab displaying the manuscript binder.
side-codex: Sidebar tab displaying character, location, and note entries.
side-codex-nav: Accessible name of the Codex navigation list.
right-panel-tabs: Accessible name of the Properties/Outline/Reference tablist.
right-panel-properties: Right-side tab that displays properties for the selected entry.
right-panel-outline: Right-side tab that displays the writer's outline.
right-panel-reference: Right-side tab that displays a reference beside the draft.
right-panel-outline-width: Accessible name of the vertical resize separator while the Outline tab is selected.
right-panel-reference-width: Accessible name of the vertical resize separator while the Reference tab is selected.
right-panel-expand: Action that expands the right-side panel.
right-panel-restore: Action that restores the right-side panel to its previous width.
right-panel-empty-properties: Empty state when no chapter or Codex entry is open in the Properties tab.
entry-place-part: Generated label for a numbered manuscript part, used in editor positions and Overview sections. $1 is a Roman numeral generated from the manuscript part number.
entry-place-not-in-sequence: Position label for a part outside the numbered sequence.
entry-place-chapter: Generated chapter position. $1 is the chapter number formatted for the interface locale.
entry-place-part-chapter: Generated position for a numbered chapter in a numbered part. $1 is the Roman part numeral; $2 is the locale-formatted chapter number.
entry-place-unsequenced-chapter: Position of a chapter in an unnumbered part. $1 is the exact isolated part title.
entry-place-unordered: Position of a chapter that cannot be ordered into the manuscript.
entry-place-character: Generated position label for a character entry.
entry-place-location: Generated position label for a location entry.
entry-place-note: Generated position label for a note entry.
entry-place-outline: Generated position label for an outline entry.
entry-place-template: Generated position label for a template entry.
entry-place-template-title-character: Generated visible document title for the character template. Never use for an author-written title.
entry-place-template-title-location: Generated visible document title for the location template. Never use for an author-written title.
entry-place-template-title-note: Generated visible document title for the note template. Never use for an author-written title.
binder-empty-copy: Empty-manuscript guidance; proposes the existing first chapter or part action without changing project semantics.
binder-empty-new-chapter: First chapter creation action shown when the manuscript is empty.
binder-empty-new-part: First part creation action shown when the manuscript is empty.
binder-chapter-title: Placeholder and accessible name of the inline new-chapter title input.
binder-part-title: Placeholder and accessible name of the inline new-part title input.
binder-new-chapter: Action label for adding a chapter to the manuscript or current part.
binder-new-part: Action label for adding a part.
binder-not-in-sequence: Section heading for parts outside the numbered sequence; does not describe file validity.
binder-unordered: Section heading for chapters that cannot be placed in manuscript order.
binder-drop-unordered: Drop-target instruction. The chapter is removed from the book's order only; its file is retained.
binder-attention: Button opening the overview's attention items. $1 is the raw PLURAL selector; $2 is the UI-locale formatted count.
binder-count-words: Complete manuscript word-count text. $1 is the raw PLURAL selector; $2 is the displayed count (an em dash at zero, otherwise UI-locale formatted).
binder-no-status: Tooltip when a chapter has no status. Actual status tokens remain untranslated.
binder-collapse-part: Accessible name of an expanded part toggle. $1 is the exact isolated part title.
binder-expand-part: Accessible name of a collapsed part toggle. $1 is the exact isolated part title.
binder-open-part: Tooltip opening a part's prose. $1 is the exact isolated part title.
binder-new-chapter-in-part: Accessible name of the add-chapter button in a part header. $1 is the exact isolated part title.
overview-heading: Heading for the manuscript Overview view.
overview-description: Explains that the view reflects file metadata and that synopses can be edited inline.
overview-filters: Accessible name for the Overview filter group.
overview-status: Filter label for the exact user-authored chapter status.
overview-any: Filter option selecting any status or thread; not a stored value.
overview-pov: Filter label for the chapter's point of view.
overview-anyone: Point-of-view filter option selecting all characters; not a stored value.
overview-thread: Filter label for the chapter's story thread.
overview-clear-filters: Action clearing Overview filters without modifying project files.
overview-no-match: Empty state when filters exclude all chapters.
overview-filtered-count: Count of matching chapters out of all chapters in a section. $1 is the raw matching count; $2 is its UI-locale formatted form; $3 is the raw total; $4 is its UI-locale formatted form.
overview-section-chapters: Generated section heading for top-level chapters in a project without parts.
overview-no-chapters: Empty table row when an unfiltered section has no chapters.
overview-synopsis-label: Accessible name of the inline synopsis editor. $1 is the exact isolated user-written chapter title.
overview-synopsis-edit: Tooltip for the button that opens inline synopsis editing.
overview-synopsis-add: Placeholder action shown when a synopsis is empty and editable.
inspector-label: Accessible name of the chapter/part Properties inspector.
inspector-position: Accessible name for the manuscript position controls.
inspector-part: Label for a chapter's Part field and the generated kind name in move tooltips.
inspector-chapter: Generated kind name used in move tooltips; chapter values remain unchanged.
inspector-order: Label for the chapter/part order field.
inspector-no-order: Placeholder indicating that the order field has no value.
inspector-move-up-label: Visible move-up action; the arrow remains a directional icon.
inspector-move-down-label: Visible move-down action; the arrow remains a directional icon.
inspector-move-up: Accessible title for moving an entry up. $1 is a translated generated kind label.
inspector-move-down: Accessible title for moving an entry down. $1 is a translated generated kind label.
inspector-remove-order: Action removing a chapter from manuscript order without deleting its file.
inspector-remove-order-tooltip: Explains that removing a chapter's order moves it to the Unordered tray but keeps its file.
inspector-renumber-part: Action renumbering chapters in the current part.
inspector-title: Label for a part or chapter title.
inspector-title-placeholder: Title placeholder. $1 is the exact isolated current title derived from the file name.
inspector-status: Label for the chapter status field; actual status tokens are never translated.
inspector-status-not-in-list: Option label for a status not declared in the project. $1 is the exact isolated status token.
inspector-add-status: Action adding a user-authored status to the project status list. $1 is the exact isolated status token.
inspector-pov: Label for a chapter's point-of-view link field.
inspector-characters: Label for a chapter's character-link field.
inspector-location: Label for a chapter's location-link field.
inspector-threads: Label and accessible name for chapter thread toggles; user-authored thread names remain unchanged.
inspector-thread-unknown: Tooltip for a thread key absent from novel.md; the key itself is not translated.
inspector-story-date: Label for a chapter's story-date field.
inspector-day-count-placeholder: Placeholder for a day-count calendar date. $1 is the UI-locale formatted example day number.
inspector-saved-to: Saved-location sentence for an editor-owned file. $1 is the exact isolated project-relative path.
outline-inspector-description: Explains that the outline is the writer's plan and that wikilink syntax is optional. Keep [[their names]] literal; do not render it as HTML or a link.
outline-inspector-while-writing: Explains how the outline appears alongside a chapter while writing. $1 is the exact bidi-isolated keyboard shortcut; do not translate it.
template-inspector-description: Explains that a new entry copies this template and edits do not change existing entries. $1 is a translated generated entry kind, not user-authored content.
template-inspector-frontmatter-prefix: First fragment of the template properties explanation. The following literal role: token remains a code element.
template-inspector-frontmatter-middle: Fragment after the literal role: code token and before the literal type token. Keep its meaning compatible with the next fragment.
template-inspector-frontmatter-and: Conjunction between the literal type and title code tokens.
template-inspector-frontmatter-end: Final word/punctuation of the template properties explanation.
outline-panel-select-label: Accessible name of the outline selector. Its displayed title/path values remain authored and unchanged.
outline-panel-empty-description: Guidance when no outline exists. Keep [[their names]] as literal Markdown wikilink syntax; the writer's outline text is never translated.
outline-panel-start: Action creating the first writer-authored outline.
outline-panel-open-in-editor: Notice above the outline panel while the same outline is open in the main editor: the panel shows that live draft, read-only; it is not a copy and is not written by the panel.
outline-panel-loading: Loading state for a selected outline.
reference-panel-label: Accessible name and fallback header for the read-only Reference panel.
reference-panel-open-editor: Action explicitly opening the reference document in the main editor.
reference-panel-show-editor: Action returning to the editor when this reference is already open there.
reference-panel-aliases: Prefix for exact user-authored aliases; aliases themselves are not translated.
reference-panel-editor-draft: Notice that the same current editor draft is shown in the reference panel; it is not a copy and is not written by the panel.
reference-panel-retry: Action retrying a failed read-only reference load.
reference-panel-loading: Loading state for a selected reference.
reference-panel-empty-heading: Heading shown before a reference is selected.
reference-panel-empty-description: Explains how to choose a codex item or chapter reference without changing the active manuscript.
reference-panel-empty-safety: Reassures the writer that reading a reference never replaces the document being written.
inspector-story-time: Label for the free-text story-time field.
inspector-story-time-placeholder: Example free-text value for a chapter's story time.
inspector-synopsis: Label for the synopsis metadata field; synopsis text remains unchanged.
inspector-read-only: Notice that project properties are read-only.
inspector-empty: Empty state shown when no manuscript entry is open.
link-picker-remove: Accessible name for removing a link chip. $1 is the exact isolated shown link label.
link-picker-add: Placeholder for adding a link to the field.
link-picker-replace: Placeholder when replacing the sole link in the point-of-view field.
rename-offer-no-links: Rename confirmation when no project links need updating. $1 is the exact isolated new file name.
rename-offer-with-links: Rename confirmation with link effects. $1 is the exact isolated new file name; $2/$4 are raw PLURAL selectors; $3/$5 are UI-locale formatted link/file counts.
rename-offer-rename: Action confirming the pending file rename.
rename-offer-keep: Action dismissing the rename prompt and keeping the current file name.
timeline-heading: Heading for the manuscript Timeline view.
timeline-order-group: Accessible name for the reading-order/story-order selector.
timeline-reading-order: Mode that places manuscript chapters in reading order.
timeline-story-order: Mode that places dated chapters on a story-time axis.
timeline-rows-group: Accessible name for the thread/character row selector.
timeline-threads: Row mode displaying story threads; authored thread names remain unchanged.
timeline-characters: Row mode displaying manuscript characters; authored names remain unchanged.
timeline-gap-prefix: Prefix for the minimum missing-chapter run length control.
timeline-gap-suffix: Suffix for the minimum missing-chapter run length control.
timeline-gap-input-label: Accessible name for the gap-length input. $1 is the UI-locale formatted current value.
timeline-zoom-group: Accessible name for the story-order zoom selector.
timeline-zoom-day: Zoom scale displaying individual story days.
timeline-outside-order: Notice reporting chapters not included in manuscript order. $1 is the raw PLURAL selector; $2 is the UI-locale formatted count.
timeline-no-chapters: Empty state when the book contains no ordered chapters.
timeline-no-threads: Empty state when no threads appear in the timeline. Keep novel.md literal; thread names are user-authored.
timeline-no-characters: Empty state when no characters appear in chapter metadata.
timeline-reading-grid: Accessible name of the timeline reading-order grid.
timeline-earlier-title: Tooltip explaining that a chapter is earlier in story time than its predecessor.
timeline-earlier: Short visible cue for a chapter that moves backward in story time.
timeline-gap-count: Missing-chapter run length. $1 is the raw PLURAL selector; $2 is the UI-locale formatted count.
timeline-cell-label: Accessible name of a grid cell. $1 and $2 are exact isolated user-authored row/chapter names; $3 is a translated state.
timeline-cell-no: Cell state indicating the row does not appear in a chapter.
timeline-cell-pov: Cell state indicating the character is the chapter's point of view.
timeline-cell-yes: Cell state indicating the row appears in the chapter.
timeline-no-story-dates: Empty state when no chapter has a usable story date.
interactions-heading: Heading for the character co-appearance matrix view.
interactions-description: Explains what the matrix counts and how to inspect a cell.
interactions-order-group: Accessible name for the character-order selector.
interactions-order-name: Sort characters alphabetically by their authored names.
interactions-order-appearances: Sort characters by number of chapters in which they appear.
interactions-outside-order: Notice reporting chapters not included in manuscript order. $1 is the raw PLURAL selector; $2 is the UI-locale formatted count.
interactions-empty: Empty state when no characters appear in chapters; directs the writer to chapter properties.
interactions-cell-self: Accessible/title label for a character's diagonal cell. $1 is the exact isolated authored name; $2 is the raw PLURAL selector; $3 is its UI-locale formatted value.

interactions-never-together: Empty state for a selected pair with no shared chapters. $1 and $2 are exact isolated authored names.
interactions-pov: Suffix identifying whose point of view a listed chapter uses. $1 is the exact isolated authored name.

codex-inspector-appears-characters: Presentation label for the characters frontmatter key; does not translate or alter the source key.
codex-inspector-appears-location: Presentation label for the location frontmatter key; does not translate or alter the source key.
codex-inspector-other-properties: Heading for unknown or additional frontmatter properties.
codex-inspector-other-note: Explains that unknown keys and values are shown as written and must be edited in the file.
codex-inspector-remove-item: Accessible name for removing an alias/group. $1 is the exact isolated user-authored item.
codex-inspector-relationships: Heading for the character relationship editor.
codex-inspector-relationship-with: Accessible name for the relationship target selector. $1 is the UI-locale formatted one-based relationship number.
codex-inspector-relationship-who: Placeholder for selecting the other character in a relationship.
codex-inspector-relationship-remove: Accessible name for removing a relationship. $1 is the UI-locale formatted one-based relationship number.
codex-inspector-relationship-kind: Accessible name for the user-authored relationship kind input. $1 is the UI-locale formatted one-based relationship number.
codex-inspector-relationship-kind-placeh: Examples only; relationship kinds remain user-authored and untranslated.
codex-inspector-relationship-note: Accessible name for the user-authored relationship note input. $1 is the UI-locale formatted one-based relationship number.
codex-inspector-relationship-note-placeh: Placeholder for a user-authored relationship note.
codex-inspector-relationship-add: Action adding a blank relationship row; adding alone does not write project data.
codex-inspector-relationships-read-only: Explains that relationships in this file use a format the app cannot safely edit and must be changed in the file.
codex-inspector-listed-by: Heading for characters whose relationship entries refer to the current character.
codex-inspector-relationships-one-way: Explains that the listed incoming relationships are stored in the other characters' files.
codex-inspector-relationship-missing: $1 is an exact isolated user-authored relationship target that has no matching file. Do not change its value or link.
reference-open-label: Accessible name of the shared reference-panel button. $1 is the exact isolated user-written title.
reference-open-tooltip: Tooltip for the shared action opening an entry in the reference panel.
initialize-heading: Question before creating a project in a plain folder. $1 is the exact isolated folder name, not a translated title. Quotes belong to the message.
initialize-description: Explains the only file initialization creates. $1 is the isolated literal novel.md, never translated. Plot Device is the unchanged application name. Do not imply the app modifies the folder's other files.
initialize-title-label: Label of the new project's title input, not a filename.
initialize-create: Submit button to create novel.md and open the project.
initialize-back: Returns from project initialization to the welcome screen without creating a project.
initialize-inside-heading: Heading when the chosen folder is inside an existing project.
initialize-inside-description: Why initialization is refused. $1 is the exact isolated chosen folder name; $2 is the exact isolated existing project title. Both are untrusted text; do not add HTML.
initialize-open-parent: Button to open the enclosing project instead of initializing the chosen subfolder. $1 is the exact isolated project title.
initialize-contains-heading: Heading when the chosen folder contains a project below it.
initialize-contains-description: Why initialization is refused. $1 is the exact isolated OS path of the existing descendant project, not a display title. Choose another folder rather than altering or deleting files.
recents-heading: Heading of the recent-project list on the welcome screen.
recents-folder-missing: Shown in place of the path when a recent project's folder no longer exists. Its open button is disabled.
recents-remove-label: Accessible name of the recent-list removal button. $1 is the exact isolated project title. The action forgets the entry only; it never deletes files.
recents-remove-tooltip: Tooltip of the recent-list removal button. Explicitly distinguish removing an entry from deleting its folder.
view-write: Main writing view tab and native View menu command.
view-overview: Derived manuscript overview, distinct from the writer's free-form outline.
view-timeline: Timeline view tab and native menu command.
view-interactions: Character co-appearance view tab and native menu command.
close-project: Close the project and return to welcome; does not delete any files.
menu-undo: Standard native undo role; accelerator and behavior are retained.
menu-toggle-outline: Show/hide the writer's outline reading panel.
menu-about: Native About command/dialog title. Plot Device is an unchanged brand.
about-detail: Native About detail. $1 is the trusted app version, not user content. Keep license identifier and URL unchanged.
about-close: Dismiss About dialog, not the project or application.
about-project-page: Open the fixed public project URL in the external browser.
date-undated: Story-date reading with no value; also character birth dates.
date-unreadable: Short timeline tooltip summary when a date cannot be used. Detailed validation appears below the timeline.
date-invalid-short: Compact timeline column label for invalid dates.
date-undated-short: Compact timeline column label for absent dates.
date-missing: Explanation beside an undated chapter in the timeline tray.
date-without-usable: Heading for chapters whose story date is missing or invalid.
date-year-bce: $1 is the positive magnitude of a Gregorian year before year zero, ungrouped decimal digits. Keep the era distinct from the number. No automatic calendar conversion.
date-day-count: $1 is a signed story day count, not a Gregorian day of month. Story-date readings pass it ungrouped; the timeline axis passes a UI-locale formatted value. It may be negative.
date-month-year: $1 is a translated month name (long in date descriptions, short on the axis); $2 is a formatted year, possibly with an era. Reorder the whole message as needed.
date-full: $1 is day of month, $2 a translated Gregorian month name, $3 a formatted year. Include any language-specific linking preposition here.
date-range: $1 and $2 are independently formatted date endpoints. Retain each endpoint's precision; do not reverse chronological order in RTL.
date-error-not-day-number: $1 is the unusable source value, bidi-isolated by the caller. Explain integer story-day input; 14 is an example.
date-error-too-large: $1 is the unusable source value, bidi-isolated by the caller; exceeds safe integer range.
date-error-not-date: $1 is the unusable source value, bidi-isolated by the caller. YYYY, YYYY-MM and YYYY-MM-DD are canonical input syntax, not localized dates.
date-error-invalid-month: $1 is the complete source date, bidi-isolated by the caller; $2 is its invalid numeric month.
date-error-invalid-day: $1 is the source date, bidi-isolated by the caller. The day does not exist in that Gregorian month/year.
date-month-1: Gregorian January, full month name. Not the Hebrew calendar.
date-month-short-1: Compact Gregorian January name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-2: Compact Gregorian February name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-3: Compact Gregorian March name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-4: Compact Gregorian April name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-5: Compact Gregorian May name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-6: Compact Gregorian June name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-7: Compact Gregorian July name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-8: Compact Gregorian August name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-9: Compact Gregorian September name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-10: Compact Gregorian October name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-11: Compact Gregorian November name for timeline ticks.
date-month-short-12: Compact Gregorian December name for timeline ticks.
warnings-heading: Heading of the project's diagnostic warnings panel.
warnings-intro: Safety promise: warnings alone never change files. The list updates after explicit app edits or external edits.
warnings-open: $1 is a project-relative file path, bidi-isolated. Tooltip for opening the warned-about file.
warnings-means: $1 is a project-relative wikilink target, bidi-isolated. Button explicitly chooses which file an ambiguous link means.
warnings-add-quotes: Explicit action to quote YAML wikilinks; not automatic.
warnings-group-unreadable: Group heading: files the app cannot safely read/edit.
warnings-group-names: Group heading: file names containing characters that break wikilinks.
warnings-group-links: Group heading: ambiguous wikilinks with multiple matching files.
warnings-group-order: Group heading: duplicate or missing manuscript ordering.
warnings-group-types: Group heading: unrecognized frontmatter type tokens.
warnings-group-project: Group heading: project-level metadata and settings warnings.
problem-unreadable-file: Unreadable file; suggest checking OS permissions.
problem-invalid-encoding: Invalid UTF-8 file is left untouched. UTF-8 is a literal encoding name.
problem-unclosed-frontmatter: The closing --- delimiter is missing; do not translate that syntax.
problem-unparseable-frontmatter: Invalid YAML; the source is left untouched.
problem-unknown-type: $1 is an unrecognized type token, bidi-isolated. It is user data, not a translated type label.
problem-nested-project: Folder has a separate novel.md and is excluded from this project; retain the literal filename.
problem-name-breaks-links: Preserve the literal forbidden wikilink characters # ^ [ ] |; suggest rename, do not perform it.
warning-novel-unreadable-file: Whole project is read-only because novel.md cannot be read. Retain literal filename.
warning-novel-invalid-encoding: Whole project is read-only because novel.md is not UTF-8.
warning-novel-unclosed-frontmatter: Whole project is read-only because novel.md's frontmatter never closes.
warning-novel-unparseable-frontmatter: Whole project is read-only because novel.md's YAML is invalid.
warning-format-missing: Literal key format is missing from novel.md; default format version is 1.
warning-format-invalid: $1 is serialized invalid format input, bidi-isolated. Keep format as the literal key. Default version 1 does not rewrite the source.
warning-format-newer: $1 is the project's numeric format version. The app cannot write newer formats; never omit read-only status.
warning-title-invalid: Literal frontmatter key title needs text; do not translate the key.
warning-author-invalid: Literal frontmatter key author needs text; do not translate the key.
warning-settings-invalid: Literal settings key must contain a YAML mapping. Defaults are in memory only.
warning-setting-file-name-sync: $1 is the complete settings key path, $2 its serialized invalid value; both isolated. ask/always/never are literal allowed values, not UI labels.
warning-setting-boolean: $1 is the complete settings key path, $2 its serialized invalid value; both isolated. true/false are literal YAML booleans.
warning-setting-folder-mapping: $1 is the complete settings key path, $2 its serialized invalid value; both isolated. Expected mapping from entry kinds to folders.
warning-setting-visible-folder: $1 is the complete settings key path, $2 its serialized invalid value; both isolated. Folder must be project-relative and not hidden.
warning-duplicate-chapter-order: $1 is the duplicate numeric order, $2 the localized list of quoted/isolated chapter titles. Preserve all titles.
warning-duplicate-part-order: $1 is the duplicate numeric order, $2 the localized list of quoted/isolated part titles.
warning-part-without-order: $1 is a localized list of quoted/isolated titles of parts outside the numbered sequence.
warning-ambiguous-body: $1 entry title, $2 wikilink, $3 all possible target paths joined with localized alternatives, $4 example path-form wikilink. Dynamic values are bidi-isolated. This occurrence is in prose.
warning-ambiguous-key: $1 entry title, $2 wikilink, $3 literal YAML key, $4 all possible paths, $5 example path-form wikilink. Values are isolated. This occurrence is in frontmatter.
warning-unquoted-link: $1 entry title, $2 complete key: wikilink source, $3 complete corrected YAML example including quotes. All isolated. Never translate syntax or split the example.
warning-not-link: $1 entry title, $2 literal YAML key, $3 serialized unusable value, all isolated. Keep the literal example "[[Name]]".
warning-not-integer: $1 entry title, $2 literal YAML key, $3 serialized unusable value, all isolated.
warning-list: $1 accumulated title list, $2 next quoted title. Used repeatedly to join arbitrary-length lists in source order.
warning-alternatives: $1 accumulated target alternatives, $2 next isolated path. Used repeatedly; all candidates must remain visible.
warning-quoted-title: $1 is an isolated user-provided title. Add locale-appropriate quotation marks.
error-read-only: Expected save/recovery failure: project is read-only. Never imply a write succeeded.
reference-not-listed: Read-only reference cannot be loaded because it is absent from the current project listing. $1 is its exact project-relative path, isolated by the caller. Do not translate the path or imply deletion.
error-workspace-folder-not-allowed: Workspace refusal: the folder must first be authorized through the native Open folder action. Translate the action label consistently with open-folder.
error-workspace-folder-missing: Workspace folder unavailable. $1 is the exact OS folder path, directionally isolated by the caller. Do not translate the path.
error-workspace-not-project: Chosen folder is not a project. $1 is its exact isolated OS path. novel.md is the fixed project marker filename and must not be translated.
error-workspace-already-project: Initialization refusal. $1 is the exact isolated OS path of a folder already recognized as a project.
error-workspace-inside-project: Opening/initialization refusal. $1 is the exact isolated OS path of the containing project; suggest opening it instead.
error-workspace-contains-project: Initialization refusal. $1 is the exact isolated OS path of a nested project found inside the chosen folder.
workspace-unsaved-changes: Navigation safety notice: an unresolved draft prevents closing or switching the open project. Translating must not retry saving or discard text.
workspace-folder-dialog-title: Title supplied by Plot Device to the native open-or-create project-folder chooser. Translate the app-owned prompt; OS controls remain system-owned.
error-template-folder-unusable: Template opening/creation refused because its configured folder cannot be used.
error-entry-already-typed: Setting a type refused because the file is no longer listed as untyped. No change made.
error-frontmatter-links-unsafe: Explicit warning-fix/link rewrite failure: frontmatter cannot be safely changed.
error-link-needs-no-folder: $1: exact isolated link target name. Chosen path-form fix no longer applies; no link was changed.
error-key-needs-no-quotes: $1: exact isolated source key. Chosen quote fix no longer applies; no value was changed.
error-name-matches: Rename refused because the filename already matches the title; no move occurred.
error-part-required: Chapter move refused because a book with parts requires a destination part.
error-chapter-missing: Chapter move refused because the chapter is no longer in the manuscript.
error-part-missing: Move/renumber refused because the part is no longer in the manuscript.
error-file-move-failed: $1: isolated exact source path. Relocation failed; preserve the failure without inventing a technical reason.
structure-renumber-failed: $1: number of files whose renumbering failed. Those files were left unchanged; other files may have been renumbered. Use PLURAL.
structure-rename-skipped: $1: number of skipped linking files. $2: exact paths, each isolated for bidi, joined as a list. Rename succeeded but these links were not safely updated. Use PLURAL.
error-groups-not-editable: Character group edits refused because the entry is not a character or groups has an unsafe shape. groups is a literal source key. File unchanged.
error-not-a-character: Relationship edits refused because the entry is not a character.
error-manuscript-type-unreadable: $1: isolated exact project-relative path whose type is not part/chapter. Read refused.
error-codex-type-unreadable: $1: isolated exact project-relative path whose type is not character/location/note. Read refused.
relationships-cannot-edit: Relationship edit safety explanation. $1: localized failure detail, already isolated where needed. Preserve the promise that the file was left unchanged and suggestion to edit the source directly.
error-no-project: Expected failure because no project session is open.
error-invalid-request: IPC argument validation refused a manuscript/codex request.
error-manuscript-entry-not-allowed: Requested path is not in the allowed manuscript listing; request refused.
error-codex-entry-not-allowed: Requested path is not in the allowed codex listing; request refused.
error-invalid-recovery-request: Recovery IPC arguments did not validate.
error-snapshot-unavailable: Recovery baseline bytes are unavailable. Draft remains open.
error-snapshot-invalid: Snapshot frontmatter is invalid; safe recovery refused.
error-recovery-outside-project: Recovery parent resolves outside project root; publication refused.
error-recovery-nested-project: Recovery parent now belongs to a nested project. Draft remains open.
error-recovery-collisions: Filename retries exhausted. Draft remains open.
error-file-outside-project: $1 is the original path, bidi-isolated; it does not resolve inside the project.
error-file-changed: $1 is the path, bidi-isolated. Version mismatch; original not overwritten.
error-file-exists: $1 is the existing destination path, bidi-isolated.
error-file-unsafe-read: $1 path, isolated; $2 localized encoding/frontmatter problem. Reading was refused.
error-file-unsafe-write: $1 path, isolated; $2 localized encoding/frontmatter problem. Writing was refused.
error-problem-unclosed: Semantic unsafe-file reason: frontmatter delimiter never closes.
error-problem-unparseable: Semantic unsafe-file reason: YAML cannot be parsed.
error-problem-none: Semantic unsafe-file reason: no frontmatter, where it is required.
error-file-write-failed: $1 project-relative path, $2 original OS error detail; both isolated. Do not translate or discard technical detail.
error-file-create-failed: $1 project-relative path, $2 original OS error detail; both isolated. Creation failed.
error-recovery-write-failed: $1 original technical exception detail, isolated and untranslated. Recovered-copy publication failed.
error-recovery-create-failed: $1 original technical exception detail, isolated and untranslated. Exclusive publication failed.
error-frontmatter-missing: No frontmatter to edit, including recovered-template conversion.
error-frontmatter-unparseable: Frontmatter edit refused because YAML is invalid.
error-frontmatter-not-mapping: Frontmatter must be a mapping of keys; edit refused.
error-frontmatter-unsupported: $1 literal frontmatter key, isolated. Its representation cannot safely be edited.
editor-save-read-only: Editor save failure; read-only project, draft is not saved.
editor-save-missing: Editor save failure for an externally moved/deleted file.
editor-resolve-before-leaving: Navigation guard: unresolved draft must stay open until explicitly resolved.
editor-not-listed: Requested document no longer exists in the current listings.
editor-writing-close-blocked: Protected writing document cannot close until another manuscript tab is chosen with Write here. That action's label is translated in a later slice.
editor-unpin-before-closing: Pinned document must be unpinned to close.
editor-wait-navigation: Property change refused while serialized document navigation is in progress.
editor-updated-from-disk: Non-destructive notice after clean external edits loaded. Does not claim an app write.
editor-snapshot-unavailable: No baseline snapshot token; recovery refused, draft kept, no writes.
editor-recovered-not-listed: Copy was written but UI listing failed; keep draft and copy path for retry, do not claim full recovery.
editor-recovered-changed: Saved copy differs on readback; keep original draft, require inspection.
editor-recovered-saved: Explicit recovered copy succeeded; original remained untouched.
editor-disk-loaded: Explicit Use disk version succeeded by reading, never writing.
editor-changed-again: Replacement failed fresh version check; no content replaced.
editor-confirm-replace: Destructive confirmation immediately before conditional body replacement. Explain external body overwrite, current frontmatter preservation, and non-destructive recovered-copy alternative. Never weaken this warning.
app-close-confirm-unresolved-draft: Warning before closing when the open draft has unresolved changes. Clearly state the draft will be lost if closed and project files on disk will remain unchanged.
editor-prose-label: Accessible name for the CodeMirror writing surface.
editor-placeholder: Empty-editor prompt; shown only when no prose has been entered.
editor-link-tooltip: Tooltip for an inline wiki link. $1 is the exact target, isolated from surrounding direction.
editor-embed-tooltip: Tooltip for an embedded wiki link. $1 is the exact target, isolated from surrounding direction.
editor-read-only-notice: Editor banner: project is read-only, no file changes permitted.
recovery-conflict-heading: Alert heading for simultaneous draft and outside edits.
recovery-conflict-description: Safety explanation: autosave paused, replacement requires explicit confirmation, recovered copy retains captured metadata and leaves original/links untouched. Preserve all guarantees.
recovery-copy-label: Label preceding a separately bidi-isolated recovered-copy path. No path parameter so the DOM can use bdi.
recovery-use-disk: Explicit read-only action: adopt current disk text, discard unsaved draft only by this choice.
recovery-save-copy: Non-destructive action: publish a separate recovered copy, not the original.
recovery-replace-disk: Destructive action opens confirmation; ellipsis indicates another step.
recovery-missing-heading: Alert heading after external deletion or move.
recovery-missing-description: $1 is a translated entry kind, not user text or a schema token. Explain intentional outside deletion, retained draft, paused autosave, close or recover alternatives, and no recreation of original path or changes to links.
recovery-reappeared: Missing path reappeared; require explicit adoption, never resume autosave automatically.
recovery-close-leave-disk: Close draft when original reappeared; do not delete or modify it.
recovery-keep-deleted: Close draft without recreating intentionally deleted original.
recovery-kind-part: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; part of the novel.
recovery-kind-chapter: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; chapter.
recovery-kind-character: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; character profile.
recovery-kind-location: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; location profile.
recovery-kind-note: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; note.
recovery-kind-template: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; template.
recovery-kind-outline: Entry kind inside missing-file explanation; outline.
workbench-notice-unavailable: Workbench layout storage is unavailable. Layouts still work for this session. This never concerns the novel's files.
workbench-notice-invalid: Some stored workbench layouts were invalid and were left out. The novel's files are never involved.
workbench-notice-save-failed: Saving the workbench layout failed. This does not describe saving manuscript text.
workbench-layout-label: Accessible name of the layout chooser in the top bar. A layout is an arrangement of panels.
workbench-layout-write: Name of the shipped layout for writing: the binder and codex beside the page, properties, outline and reference on the other side.
workbench-layout-revise: Name of the shipped layout for revising: like Write, with the warnings panel below the page.
workbench-layout-plot: Name of the shipped layout for plotting mode, with the plot board in the middle.
workbench-panel-label: Accessible name of a side or bottom panel. $1 is the title of the view it currently shows, such as Properties.
workbench-resize-panel: Accessible name of a vertical resize separator beside a side panel. $1 is the title of the view the panel shows.
workbench-resize-shelf: Accessible name of the horizontal resize separator above the bottom panel.
workbench-section-collapse: Button that collapses one view in a panel. $1 is the view's title.
workbench-section-expand: Button that expands one collapsed view in a panel. $1 is the view's title.
menu-classic-layout: View menu command that switches between the workbench and the previous fixed panel layout.
workbench-panel-options: Accessible name of the ⋯ button for one view in a panel. $1 is the view's title.
workbench-area-options: Accessible name of the ⋯ button for a whole side or bottom panel.
workbench-move-left: Moves a view to the panel on the left of the screen. Names the physical side, which already accounts for right-to-left layout.
workbench-move-right: Moves a view to the panel on the right of the screen. Names the physical side, which already accounts for right-to-left layout.
workbench-move-bottom: Moves a view to the panel below the page.
workbench-move-earlier: Moves a view one place earlier among the views in its panel (toward the reading start).
workbench-move-later: Moves a view one place later among the views in its panel.
workbench-section-close: Removes a view from the layout. $1 is the view's title. The view can be shown again from the layout menu; nothing in the novel changes.
workbench-add-view: Adds a view to this panel. $1 is the view's title.
workbench-show-view: Layout menu item that places a view the layout doesn't show yet in its usual panel. $1 is the view's title.
workbench-show-tabs: Shows a panel's views one at a time, as tabs.
workbench-show-stacked: Shows a panel's views all at once, one above the other.
workbench-layout-options: Accessible name of the ⋯ button beside the layout chooser.
workbench-layout-save-as: Starts saving the current arrangement under a new name.
workbench-layout-rename: Starts renaming the writer's own layout.
workbench-layout-delete: Starts deleting the writer's own layout. Only the arrangement is deleted, never any file.
workbench-layout-delete-confirm: Confirms deleting a layout. $1 is the layout's name, written by the writer.
workbench-layout-reset: Returns a shipped layout to its original arrangement.
workbench-layout-name: Label of the field for a layout's name.
workbench-layout-save: Saves a layout under the typed name.
workbench-layout-cancel: Leaves the layout name or delete step without changes.
workbench-layout-name-empty: Shown when a layout name is empty.
workbench-layout-name-too-long: Shown when a layout name is too long. A letter with its vowel marks counts as one character.
workbench-layout-name-taken: Shown when another layout has the same name, ignoring letter case. $1 is that name.
cards-stack-title: Title of the panel that holds pinned entry cards.
cards-empty: Shown in the empty card stack. Explains the two ways to pin a card.
cards-pin: Button that pins the shown entry as a card in the card stack.
cards-pin-label: Accessible name of the pin button. $1 is the entry's title, written by the writer.
cards-unpin-label: Removes a pinned card from the stack. $1 is the entry's title. Nothing in the novel changes.
cards-collapse: Collapses a card to one line. $1 is the entry's title.
cards-expand: Expands a collapsed card. $1 is the entry's title.
cards-options: Accessible name of a card's ⋯ menu. $1 is the entry's title.
cards-move-up: Moves a card one place up in the stack.
cards-move-down: Moves a card one place down in the stack.
cards-field-show: Card menu item that adds a field to every card of this kind. $1 is the field's label, such as Role.
cards-field-hide: Card menu item that removes a field from every card of this kind. $1 is the field's label.
cards-peek-label: Accessible name of the preview card shown for a link. $1 is the linked entry's title.
cards-loading: Shown in a card while the entry is read.
cards-live-draft: Note on a card whose entry is open in the main editor: the card shows that live draft, read-only.
cards-list-separator: Separator between values of one card field, such as two aliases. Keep the trailing space if your language uses one.
cast-label: Title of the strip above the page listing the characters and places the chapter being written names, and of that view in panel menus.
cast-hide: Removes the cast strip from above the page. It can be shown again from the layout menu; nothing in the novel changes.
cast-chip-pov: Accessible name of a cast chip for the chapter's point-of-view character. $1 is the character's title.
cast-chip-mentioned: Accessible name of a cast chip for a character or place the chapter's text links to but its properties don't list. $1 is the entry's title.
cast-empty: Shown in the cast strip when the chapter names nobody, in its properties or its text.
scene-card-title: Title of the panel describing the chapter being written: its synopsis, status, point of view, threads, and the outline lines about it.
scene-card-in-outline: Heading above the outline lines that link to the chapter being written.
scene-card-no-chapter: Shown in the chapter panel when no chapter is being written or open.
scene-card-no-outline-lines: Shown when no line of the current outline links to the chapter being written.
scene-card-edit: Opens the chapter in the editor and shows its Properties panel, where its synopsis and status can be changed.
split-open-beside: Action that shows a document read-only beside the editor, to compare it with the one being written.
split-open-beside-label: Accessible name of the Open beside action. $1 is the document's title, written by the writer.
split-read-only: Label on a split beside the editor: it can't be edited there. Use Write here to edit it.
split-lock: Toggle that keeps a split's document when the writer opens other documents beside. Pressed while locked.
split-close: Closes the read-only split beside the editor. Nothing in the novel changes.
split-empty: Shown in an empty split beside the editor.
split-all-locked: Shown when Open beside can't find a split: there are already two and both are locked.
split-region: Accessible name of a read-only split. $1 is the title of the document it shows.
split-resize: Accessible name of the separator that resizes a split beside the editor.
menu-command-palette: View menu command that opens the command palette (Ctrl+K), for going to any entry, view, layout or command by typing.
palette-title: Accessible name of the command palette dialog.
palette-placeholder: Placeholder in the command palette's search field.
palette-count: Announced count of matching palette items. $1 is the raw PLURAL selector; $2 is the UI-locale formatted number.
palette-empty: Shown when no palette item matches what was typed.
palette-kind-view: Label beside a palette item that shows a view, such as Timeline.
palette-kind-layout: Label beside a palette item that switches to a layout.
palette-kind-command: Label beside a palette item that runs a command, such as toggling the binder.
palette-beside-hint: Hint under the palette's list. $1 is the keyboard shortcut (Shift+Enter), shown as is.
palette-use-layout: Palette item that switches to a layout. $1 is the layout's name, translated for shipped layouts or written by the writer.
appearance-fade: Writing appearance option: while typing, the panels and bars fade, and return when the pointer moves.
